title: Workspace trust dialog gets stuck
body: After updating Helix to 25.07.1 (253e6195) from source on macOS, making a Git commit with `hx` configured as `core.editor` opens Helix with a workspace trust dialog. In the native macOS Terminal 2.15 (466), arrow keys and other keyboard buttons do nothing, so I cannot make a selection. The only new Helix log line says that building syntax for `~/.cache/helix/helix.log` exceeded the configured timeout.

symptoms_visible: When Git opens Helix 25.07.1 (253e6195) in the native macOS Terminal, the workspace trust dialog appears but arrow keys and other keyboard buttons do nothing, so I cannot select anything.
N0.label: N0 trust dialog accepts no input

symptoms_visible: Escape, number keys, arrow keys, and arbitrary letters all do nothing.
The same loss of keyboard input happens every time I open a file in Helix, including the Helix log file.
N1.label: N1 input loss is not limited to Git or menu keys

symptoms_visible: With `editor.insecure = true`, the trust dialog no longer appears, but the native Terminal tab still accepts no keyboard input after Helix starts.
N2_x.label: N2_x disabling trust dialog aftermath

symptoms_visible: The instrumented build writes no key-event lines while I press keys in the stuck native macOS Terminal.
The same Helix version works on my home Linux machine and in iTerm2 on macOS.
On another affected Linux setup, Helix works when launched directly but accepts no input when launched inside aerc's sub-terminal.
N3.label: N3 failure narrowed to particular terminal interactions

symptoms_visible: The provided candidate branch starts normally in the native macOS Terminal, and the terminal no longer gets stuck.
N4.label: N4 candidate branch avoids the stall

symptoms_visible: In an affected aerc session, pressing Escape, pausing, and then pressing backslash makes the stuck Helix session start accepting input.
N5.label: N5 parser can be manually resynchronized

symptoms_visible: With the latest master build, the workspace trust dialog responds to the keyboard normally in the native macOS Terminal and no longer gets stuck.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved on latest master

question_patterns: Does an unhandled key such as Escape, a number, or an arbitrary letter close the menu?
Are only the arrow keys ignored, or does the terminal ignore every key?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Nothing happens. Escape does nothing, number keys do nothing, arrow keys do nothing, and arbitrary letters do nothing.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Letters and Escape work normally; only the arrow keys fail to move the selection.
Every tested key is ignored, including Enter as well as Escape, numbers, arrows, and letters.

question_patterns: Does this happen only while editing a Git commit message?
Can you open and edit an ordinary file outside Git?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It happens every time I open a file in Helix, even when I open the Helix log file.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It only happens when Git launches Helix; opening the same files directly works normally.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c1 and c3: all keys are ignored, and the problem is not specific to Git commit editing.

solution.intent: Disable workspace trust prompts by setting the editor's insecure option.
solution.concrete_example: Add `[editor] insecure = true` to the Helix configuration so the trust dialog is skipped.

edges.comment: Maintainer suggestion c4 and reporter result c7: the persistent configuration change removes the dialog but leaves the terminal tab unable to receive input, so it does not solve the underlying problem.

question_patterns: Can you run the provided diagnostic branch and check whether pressing keys produces `KeyEvent` warning lines in the Helix log?
Please test the instrumented build, press several keys while it is stuck, and paste any new key-event log entries.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried the provided diagnostic branch and apparently no keys are logged when I press them.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every key press appears in the log as a normal `KeyEvent`, even while the dialog remains unresponsive.
I tried several letters and arrow keys; none of them produced a key-event log line.

question_patterns: Does another affected terminal or nested TUI setup show the same loss of input?
Can the issue be reproduced when another TUI launches Helix inside a sub-terminal?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I also hit this with Helix 25.07.1 on Linux when aerc launches it inside its sub-terminal. Helix works when I launch it in isolation, but inside aerc the trust dialog accepts no input; trusting `/tmp` removes the dialog and Helix still receives no input.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Helix works normally in aerc and every other nested terminal; only one standalone macOS session is affected.
The aerc color theme is different from the Helix theme.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c8-c10 and c13 establish that the diagnostic build receives no key events, while Linux direct launch and iTerm2 work. The aerc evidence and screenshot come from affected user rcorre in c11-c12 and are explicitly folded into the simulated affected-user side; it is a separate environment exhibiting the same terminal-input stall, not a replacement for the reporter's macOS setup.

question_patterns: Could you build and test this candidate branch in the default macOS Terminal and report whether it still gets stuck?
Please try the provided branch in the same native Terminal setup and tell me whether keyboard input works.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I believe the provided branch fixes it. The macOS Terminal app no longer gets stuck while I am using that branch.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The candidate branch gets stuck in exactly the same way in the native macOS Terminal.
The candidate branch works in the native macOS Terminal, although I only tested opening a regular file rather than a Git commit.

edges.comment: Maintainer request c14 and reporter result c18: this is a pre-landing candidate-branch measurement. The reporter reports only that the branch avoids the stall; identifying the OSC interaction as causal remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: When Helix hangs, can you press Escape, pause, then press backslash and report what happens?
Can you try the suggested recovery key sequence in an affected session?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When Helix hangs inside aerc, I press Escape, wait briefly, and press backslash; after that it starts responding.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Escape followed by backslash has no effect; the session remains unable to receive input.
The sequence works, but only if I pause briefly between Escape and backslash.

edges.comment: Affected user jshholland's c21 IRC test is folded into the user side. The raw observation is only that the key sequence recovers the session; the conclusion about an unterminated terminal response and parser resynchronization is engineer analysis.

solution.intent: Fix the terminal-response parser so an OSC color-query response terminated in the alternate supported form cannot leave Helix waiting indefinitely and swallowing subsequent keyboard input.
solution.concrete_example: Update the termina parser to accept the terminal's OSC response terminator instead of remaining stuck waiting for a different terminator, then ask the reporter to retest a current master build in the native macOS Terminal.
solution.inference_hint: The affected users supplied environment comparisons, absence of key-event logs, candidate-build behavior, and the Escape-then-backslash recovery. Maintainers inferred that the OSC 11 response used a terminator different from the one Helix's terminal parser was waiting for, leaving the parser stuck and consuming later input. The final accepted fix was parser-side handling of the response terminators, not merely hiding the trust dialog or permanently avoiding the query.

edges.comment: Final technical chain from c21-c25: the recovery sequence exposed the parser synchronization problem; xe-nul implemented the termina change, reported it in master, and the original macOS reporter then verified current master in the native Terminal. Confirmations from aerc users in c27-c28 are corroborating evidence, while the reporter's own c25 and c29 establish resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: an OSC 11 terminal response used a terminator that Helix's terminal parser did not accept in that state, leaving the parser waiting and preventing subsequent keyboard input from reaching the editor.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: no key events were logged, direct launches worked in other terminals, the candidate branch avoided the stall, and Escape followed by backslash could recover an affected nested-terminal session.

Must fix or resynchronize the terminal parser so it handles the relevant OSC response terminators; disabling workspace trust with `editor.insecure = true` is not a fix because the terminal remained stuck after the dialog disappeared.

Must not characterize the problem as inherently limited to the workspace trust dialog or to macOS, because it occurred for ordinary files and was also reproduced when aerc launched Helix in a Linux sub-terminal.
Must ask the reporter to verify a build containing the parser fix in the native macOS Terminal and only declare resolution after that verification.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Helix user who builds from source, edits configuration, uses Git and fish, can switch terminal emulators, pull diagnostic branches, and inspect logs; additional affected aerc users are folded into the user side for the nested-terminal evidence.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise, cooperative, and empirical; reports exact observations, tries proposed branches and configuration changes, and distinguishes tentative results with phrasing such as 'apparently' and 'I believe'.
